steps.what: Explain artistic techniques and demonstrate their execution while responding to student questions

tasks.design: Keep live explanation and demonstration with the teacher. Reference materials in {LMS} support the class, but their existing availability does not reduce the demonstrated technique or responsive explanation.
tasks.previous_blocker: Technique involves embodied performance and immediate adaptation to learners.
tasks.enabler_now: Digital examples already supplement teaching without replacing it.
tasks.still_hard: Making tacit choices visible and responding to a student's misunderstanding.
tasks.human_edge: Demonstrating nuance and adjusting the example in the moment.
tasks.altitude: Teaching time and responsibility remain unchanged.

reach.learn: Observe technique without imposing one artistic interpretation

evidence.claim: Live artistic explanation and demonstration remain human work in this design; the digest establishes no replacement or measured time benefit.

assumptions: Boundary is delivering the explanation and demonstration, not lesson-material production or student assessment.
No structured-input contract or machine action is introduced.
Native learning-material access is sufficient; no custom build.
Zero incremental upkeep because tools and teaching procedures stay unchanged.
unknowns: Art discipline and mode of teaching
research_questions: Which techniques need live demonstrations because static examples fail to show the process?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100; gross0 minus upkeep0 = net0. No shorter demonstration or invented preparation saving.

steps.what: Evaluate class work, performances, projects or papers against the assessment criteria
Write feedback explaining the evaluation using observed examples

loop.purpose: Draft feedback wording from the examiner's observations
loop.input: Teacher-written observations, criteria and provisional grade
loop.output: Draft explanation with references to observed examples
loop.check: Teacher verifies each claim, artistic nuance and consistency with the actual performance or work
loop.stop: Unsupported interpretation or distorted criticism returns to manual writing after two drafts
loop.why_not_simpler: Individual feedback needs contextual language; the model does not view or grade the work

steps.what: Check feedback, decide the final grade and release the exact result

tasks.design: Test native rubric and feedback templates in {LMS}. A bounded loop can draft wording from teacher observations, while the teacher retains the entire artistic evaluation and final grade decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: Writing a useful explanation takes effort after the substantive evaluation.
tasks.enabler_now: Feedback drafting from instructor notes is available without delegating the grade.
tasks.still_hard: Preserving artistic nuance and avoiding generic or unjustified criticism.
tasks.human_edge: Recognising artistic intent, technical development and contextual merit.
tasks.altitude: Potentially less wording effort; examiner rights and responsibility remain unchanged.

evidence.claim: D2L Brightspace Lumi Feedback drafts text and rubric feedback from instructor notes; this does not establish artistic grading validity.
The proposed arts-feedback time range is unmeasured and does not transfer physics or essay-study results.

assumptions: Boundary includes evaluation, explanatory feedback and final result release, not teaching or maintaining duplicate registers.

Arts teacher produces learner and assignment references, criterion-linked observations, concrete examples, uncertainty and provisional grades in s1; all65 hours include note capture. No structured evaluation or recording appears for free.

For written or recorded work the evaluation means may be document or screen instead of live observation; all work is still evaluated by the teacher. Missing observation detail returns to manual feedback within s2.
Native templates precede a loop. Model drafting never supplies a new score or artistic judgement.
unknowns: Actual share of time spent wording feedback
research_questions: Does checking drafted feedback retain the teacher's intended nuance while reducing wording effort?

approvals.approved_version: Exact final grade and corrected feedback for the named submission; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R92 gives gross8 minus upkeep3 = net5. Low assumes meaning checks consume the full feedback-writing baseline; high requires40% saving in the20-hour wording step, with artistic evaluation and final grading unchanged.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Prepare students for performance and assessment

steps.what: Identify performance or assessment requirements and the student's preparation needs
Prepare students through rehearsal, coaching and practice feedback for performances or exams

tasks.design: Keep preparation needs and coaching with the teacher. Requirements in {DOCS} guide rehearsal, but generated advice does not replace responsive practice feedback.
tasks.previous_blocker: Preparation depends on the student's actual performance and confidence.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reference materials help clarify requirements without changing contact work.
tasks.still_hard: Performance anxiety and making technical corrections without suppressing artistic choices.
tasks.human_edge: Judging readiness and providing appropriate encouragement and challenge.
tasks.altitude: No change to coaching time or readiness judgement.

evidence.claim: The design preserves individual preparation and coaching; no arts-specific coaching time benefit is established in the digest.

assumptions: Boundary is targeted performance or exam preparation, not general technique instruction, examination or scheduling. Overlapping teaching contact must be assigned once in roll-ups.
No machine preparation plan consumes an assumed structured student profile.
Use existing requirement documents before any build; no new software proposed.
Zero upkeep because teaching practice and tools remain unchanged.
unknowns: Preparation format and learner support needs
research_questions: What preparation barriers require an individual rehearsal response?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gives net0 after zero upkeep. Readiness judgement and rehearsal remain fully counted.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Initiate, facilitate and moderate classroom discussions while responding to students' ideas

tasks.design: Retain live moderation and participation with the teacher and students. Readings in {LMS} can support discussion, but no new tool replaces listening and facilitation.
tasks.previous_blocker: The next useful question depends on the emerging conversation.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing learning-material access supports the class without removing moderation.
tasks.still_hard: Balancing participation and handling disagreement about sensitive interpretations.
tasks.human_edge: Inviting quieter students and challenging ideas constructively.
tasks.altitude: No change to facilitation time or responsibility.

evidence.claim: Live discussion facilitation remains human work; no automation saving is claimed.

assumptions: Boundary is live discussion, not preparing readings, writing lesson plans or assessing participation.
No transcript, emotion inference or structured participation score is introduced.
Native material access is enough; no custom build.
Zero upkeep because the discussion process continues unchanged.
research_questions: Which participation barriers can the teacher address through facilitation?

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100; net0 after zero upkeep. No preparation or transcription baseline is invented.

role.altitude: Arts teachers retain embodied teaching, critique and grading; only wording of evidence-based feedback is tested for savings.
reach: Coordinate moderation with assessment staff and rehearsal conditions with performance coordinators
role.ambitious_version: Accountable arts education with precise feedback and full human attention to performance and interpretation.
